title: Error, TypeError, and custom errors
hook: JavaScript signals failure by throwing values — almost always Error objects with message and stack. Built-in subclasses classify bugs (TypeError, ReferenceError), and custom errors carry domain context for APIs and logs.

blocks.text: **throw** stops normal execution and unwinds the call stack until a matching **catch** or the runtime reports an uncaught exception. The idiomatic thrown value is an **Error** instance: `.message` for humans, `.stack` for frames, `.name` for the constructor (e.g. TypeError). **Error.cause** (ES2022) chains a root failure like C# InnerException. You can throw any value (`throw "oops"`), but only Error gives reliable stacks in production.

entries.plainDefinition: Base built-in error type with message and stack.
Operation on wrong type — undefined is not a function, etc.
Invalid identifier reference — undeclared variable or TDZ.
Optional chained error passed as { cause } in constructor options.

blocks.text: API layers map HTTP status to typed errors (NotFoundError, ValidationError). Logging pipelines rely on `.stack` and structured `.name`. Throwing strings loses stack frames. C# requires Exception-derived types for idiomatic catch filters; JavaScript uses **instanceof** branches inside a single catch.

blocks.title: Always throw Error
blocks.body: throw new Error(msg) — not throw msg. For domain errors, subclass Error and set this.name in constructor.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Evaluate throw expression
items.body: Any value can be thrown; Error recommended.

items.title: Unwind stack
items.body: Each frame pops until catch found or top-level uncaught.

items.title: catch receives value
items.body: Branch with err instanceof TypeError, custom classes, or err.code.

items.title: Log and rethrow
items.body: Add context then throw new Error("...", { cause: err }) for observability.

snippet.label: Built-in error types
snippet.explanation: TypeError for wrong type; RangeError for numeric domain violation. stack helps locate call site.

snippet.label: Custom error subclass
snippet.explanation: Subclass sets name for logs and monitoring. status property enables catch routing without string parsing.

snippet.label: Error.cause chains
snippet.explanation: Outer error adds context; cause preserves root failure for debugging — mirrors InnerException.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: throw "string" without stack. Forgetting to set name on custom errors. Catching and swallowing without log. Using generic Error when status/code enables recovery. Not preserving cause when rethrowing.

interviewTakeaways: Throw Error objects — message, name, stack; avoid bare strings.
TypeError, ReferenceError, RangeError classify common failure modes.
Subclass Error for domain types; use instanceof in catch.
Error.cause chains root failures like InnerException.
60s: throw Error not string. Built-in subclasses. Custom class with name. cause for wrap. instanceof not typed catch.
commonPitfalls: Weak: "throw works like return with a string." Strong: "throw unwinds stack; Error gives stack trace; strings lose frames."
Weak: "catch (TypeError e) in JS." Strong: "Single catch; if (err instanceof TypeError) { ... } — TS has no typed catch."
Strong: "Show HttpError with status + cause chain for API layer — production pattern."

jsTsCorrelations.note: TypeScript types custom errors with class extends Error; use type guards (instanceof) after catch (err: unknown).
C# catch filters use when on typed exceptions; JavaScript emulates with instanceof and err.code properties.
